question: Each successive rally in this chart reaches a higher price high, but volume is lighter on each rally. What is the most appropriate interpretation?
options: The advance is confirmed and buying pressure is increasing
Lighter volume shows sellers are absent, which confirms the advance
It signals an immediate reversal, so the position should be reversed short now
Demand is weakening beneath the uptrend, a warning that the trend may be nearing exhaustion

question: Price makes a higher high at the end of the chart while On-Balance Volume makes a lower high. What is the best interpretation?
options: A bullish confirmation: OBV is still well above its starting level, so accumulation remains intact and the higher price high is validated
A bearish divergence: volume flow is not confirming the new price high, warning of distribution
A bullish divergence, because OBV fell while price rose, implying sellers are exhausted
No signal, because OBV only matters when it crosses its own zero line

question: After an extended decline, Stock KLM trades on about 5.2× its average volume with a wide range and a close well off the low, followed by a sharp bounce. What is this, and what would best confirm a durable low?
options: A selling climax; a bottom is better confirmed if a later retest of the low area occurs on much lighter volume and holds above the climax low
A selling climax; a bottom is confirmed only if the retest undercuts the climax low on even heavier volume
A breakaway move lower; the heavy volume confirms a new leg of the downtrend has begun
A blow-off top; the long lower shadow shows that supply is now overwhelming demand

question: Two closes above resistance are marked A and B. Using the breakout-day volume relative to its 20-day average (values annotated), which breakout carried stronger volume confirmation?
options: Breakout A, because a breakout on light volume (0.8× average) shows there are few sellers left
Breakout B, at about 2.0× average volume, though volume is irrelevant to breakout validity
Breakout B, at about 2.4× average volume; A came on below-average volume and lacked conviction
Both equally, since each produced a close above resistance

question: Average volume is annotated for each swing leg (red = declining legs, green = rebounds). What does the volume pattern say about the trend?
options: Volume expands on declines and contracts on rebounds, confirming the downtrend; rebounds look corrective
Heavy volume on each decline signals capitulation, so the downtrend is likely complete
Light volume on rebounds shows sellers are absent, a bullish sign that the trend is turning
Volume is not informative in downtrends because prices can fall of their own weight
